content: Before initiating oral microbiota therapy, it is essential to complete any ongoing antibiotic regimens 2 to 4 days in advance. This precaution is necessary because oral microbiota products contain bacterial spores, and the concurrent use of antibacterial agents can reduce their efficacy. The reduction in efficacy occurs due to pharmacodynamic antagonism between the antibiotics and the bacterial spores in the microbiota product. Specific antibiotics, such as gentamicin, iclaprim, imipenem/cilastatin, kanamycin, lefamulin, levofloxacin, lincomycin, linezolid, meropenem, meropenem/vaborbactam, methenamine, methenamine/sodium salicylate/benzoic acid, metronidazole (vaginal), minocycline, moxifloxacin, nafcillin, neomycin (PO), nitrofurantoin, norfloxacin, ofloxacin, omadacycline, oritavancin, oxacillin, penicillin G (aqueous), penicillin G benzathine, penicillin G procaine, penicillin VK, piperacillin, plazomicin, polymyxin B, quinupristin/dalfopristin, relebactam, retapamulin, rifamycin, rifaximin, sarecycline, streptomycin, sulbactam/durlobactam, sulfadiazine, sulfanilamide, sulfisoxazole, sulopenem, sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid, tebipenem, tedizolid, telavancin, tetracycline, tigecycline, tobramycin, and trimethoprim, have been shown to decrease the effects of oral microbiota therapy through this mechanism. To ensure the success of oral microbiota therapy, it is recommended to avoid or use alternative drugs to these antibiotics during the treatment period. If the use of these antibiotics is unavoidable, their administration should be completed at least 2 to 4 days before starting oral microbiota therapy. This approach minimizes the risk of reduced efficacy of the microbiota product and allows the bacterial spores to colonize effectively.
